nyhavn: The harbour canal with its colourful 17th- and 18th-century houses and old wooden boats moored alongside, the most famous image of Copenhagen. Hans Christian Andersen lived here in three different houses. The south (sunny) side has restaurants and bars with outdoor tables; the north side is quieter for a stroll.
christians: The palace on the islet of Slotsholmen, seat of the Danish Parliament and where the King receives state guests. You can visit the Royal Reception Rooms with tapestries telling the country's history, the ruins of older castles beneath the palace and the royal kitchens. The palace tower is the city's tallest, and the climb is free.
amalien: Amalienborg and the changing of the guard

The royal family's winter residence: four 18th-century palaces around a great octagonal square with the equestrian statue of Frederik V. Part of it is a museum, with the private apartments of 19th- and 20th-century kings and queens, the jewel room and the reception rooms. Nearby is the Marble Church with its great dome.
rosenb: Rosenborg Castle and the Crown Jewels

A 17th-century red-brick Renaissance castle built by King Christian IV as a country residence, now surrounded by the Danes' favourite park, Kongens Have. Inside are rooms with the original furniture and thrones and, in the basement, the treasury with the crown jewels and regalia.
rund: A cylindrical tower from 1642 that King Christian IV built as the university's astronomical observatory. Instead of steps there's a wide spiral ramp which, the story goes, a carriage once drove up. At the top, the terrace looks over the green roofs of the centre. Around it are the oldest lanes and Strøget, the long pedestrian shopping street.
tivoli: One of the world's oldest amusement parks (1843), in the middle of the city, with gardens, ponds, Chinese pavilions, a 1914 wooden roller coaster and lots of lights in the evening. After sunset is the best time. Walt Disney drew inspiration from it for Disneyland.
natmus: The country's largest history museum, close to Christiansborg: the Vikings, Bronze Age jewellery and weapons, the famous Trundholm Sun Chariot, collections from Greenland and the Arctic. There's also a children's section.
kastell: A 17th-century star-shaped fortress, now a park with grassy ramparts, the old windmill and the soldiers' red houses. Along the water, 10 minutes' walk away, is the Little Mermaid, the small bronze statue recalling Andersen's fairy tale. It's small: many people are disappointed, but the harbour walk is lovely.
christiansh: Christianshavn, Church of Our Saviour and Christiania

A canal district inspired by Amsterdam, with low houses, bridges and boats. The Church of Our Saviour (Vor Frelsers Kirke) has a Baroque spire with an external spiral staircase you can climb to the top for a view over the whole city. A few steps away is Christiania, a self-governing area founded in 1971 in a former barracks, with murals, workshops and alternative bars.
torve: Two glass market halls near Nørreport station with over 60 stalls: smørrebrød (Danish open sandwiches), fresh fish, cheese, pastries, coffee and fruit. The best place for a quick lunch or a few tastings.
glypt: An art museum near Tivoli with Egyptian, Greek and Roman sculpture and a fine collection of French Impressionists, founded by the brewer Carl Jacobsen. The Winter Garden at the centre of the building, with palms and a fountain, is a peaceful place to pause.
